REVIEW_BODY: This is a wonderful place made up of man stalls vending all kinds of foods, sweets, desserts and drinks. It's inviting and gun.
This is a must if you are in Madrid, the food is good the drinks even better. Sure there are a lot of fellow tourist, is an opportunity too meet great people.
A little market of tapas. A must if you like tapas. Price were pretty much €1/tapas. Not that bad but probably not if you're really hungry.

A must do when you visit Madrid. Lots of really good food and the wine is cheap but very nice. A gin and tonic did set us back over 15e but it was quite big! Wish there was s place like this near where i live as it is so laid back, atmosphere great and a fab way to spend an evening
A good place to simply stroll in and have a bite to eat. Lots to choose from and the place is happening. In a great part of town that you will likely be visiting, so easy to plan this place in.

One of the best places in Madrid to taste the local gastronomy. Located near the Plaza Mayor, offers great variety of food at better prices than the restaurants around the Plaza. Don't miss the seafood tapas with sangria of course.
Fun, busy market with a huge variety of food and drinks. Many tapas and drinks in a fun and lively atmosphere! Definitely worth checking out!
A nice place to grab a piece of food and a drink. Many places to choose from. Be aware that there are a lot of people around.
Lots of different foods under one roof. We loved the churros and hot chocolate. It's close to Plaza Mayor so it's worth visiting them at the same time.
Nothing to do with a Mercado. The counters are all individual restaurants with various food selections. Beautifully displayed, outrageously priced. Crowded and uncomfortable.

Every time I'm in Madrid I need to stop there. i always loved the place. The atmosphere is amazing, especially in the evening. You can try any type of local food you want. Prices are not cheap but most of the products are good quality! You can go from one booth to the other one trying a bit of everything. Make sure you stop tjere during your trip to Madrid!
Quaint market pales in comparison to Barcelona markets but excellent food fun and atmosphere. Located at the center of the action. A must see in Madrid.

Passed by twice in a week, but in vain. MM is a very nice looking place, but super busy and not with the most attentive service.
Gave up and found another place in the alley between MM and Plaza Mayor.

A wonderful selection of fresh Spanish food and drink. It was busy around lunchtime and difficult, if not impossible, to find a seat, but there are standing locations by the bar or around the sides of the market so if you're happy to stand and eat it's fine. Great fresh seafood, ham and cheese. Also loved the fresh fruit juices and fruit pots. Yum!

Nothing can prepare you for the extraordinary display of food and drink gathered in this one space.A glorious expedition into Olives of every kind stuffed with hams and cheeses and fish and many other delights to enjoy.Fish that I have never seen before.Sangria and Cava and lots of great Spanish wines.Without eating anything you will enjoy the experience.However ,you will partake as do we all.Enjoy all of it.

A nice piece of iron architecture but otherwise touristy and busy.
Better go to market uptown in authentic neighbourhood if you want to see the real deal.

If you are willing to work your way through crowds and wait for limited seating for tasty tapas, then you'll enjoy the Mercado. Under one roof you'll find different booths/stations of various tapas and drinks. A great way to experience most of the typical Spanish foods, e.g. olives, paella, tortilla de Espanola, and of course, tinto or sangria. Be on the watch out for vacant seating in the middle. They go fast.

Our guided tour suggested this market for us and it provided something for everyone. Sometimes on our vacations food options can be complicated because everyone wants something different. This is why this is a great option. Not only can each person go somewhere different but you can also buy every course from a different vendor. I got white wine from one shop, a ham sandwich from another, and fries from another as well as dessert, ice cream, from another. However, keep a receipt as you will need if you wish to use the restroom here.

In addition to the food, the setting is well designed and built. It is a great building to house the different vendors but to do it in such a way that you were not hot. Also is well located adjacent to the western exit from Plaza Mayor.

I highly recommend the market and I recommend visiting as many different vendors to take full advantage of the variety.
Excellent place to try local food and treats. Great variety of jams, pastries tapas, wines and just about anything you can think of from Spain and more. The perfect place to hang out with friends.
A fantastic environment in which to eat drink and socialise! There is something there for everyone and I would particularly recommend the lovely choice of wines and sangria!

Teaming with wonderful food and drink, this place is a must see venue in Madrid. Shame there aren't more places to sit but leaning up against a counter in the great ambience is fun, unless you have been on your feet all day! Very reasonably priced too!

We read about this fabulous place, and were so delighted to visit. It was like a wonderful dream!!!

Each vendor had added a special touch for our eyes to feast on.
The food was good but expensive. Very crowded and tense atmosphere. Poor attention to patrons - hard to place order .
Amazing foods - you will want to eat everything. They all look so appetising. It gets very crowded so perhaps it's better to go either very early or a bit later. Everything is inexpensive

推荐如果你正在寻找典型的产品，各种各样的传统菜肴，如果你没有时间吃饭我会说这是伟大的

Recommended if you are looking for typical products, great variety of traditional dishes, if you have little time to eat I would say it's great
Great food available in this eat in or take away food market- busy and atmospheric . We had some alcoholic beverages and snacks - different and tasty

Anyone looking to stuff their faces with food needs to go here. I love this place it’s full of market stalls selling wine cheese jamon basically everything. It’s a must visit if you love food. I have to go every time I’m in Madrid

We went there on Sunday evening and it was not very busy so it was great to be there with my son in a stroller. We had the best sangria and fresh oyster. The rest of the food was just ok. Nothing so special. Maybe I was expecting too much as we always have good meal in Madrid since day 1 of our visit. But you have to come here for the experience.
This restored cover market hosted mostly tourists. The selection of wines and tapas on offer is varied and one can get tapas from €1 and wine by the glass from €3.

This market is very famous in madrid, because of the fresh product that you can find. Depending on day it could be really crowded, but you can spend 20 minutes to walk it and taste some tapas. The prices are a little bit high cause of the quality. It is also next to plaza mayor, so you can visit both places in the same walk.

Tapas, Tapas & Tapas,...you can find here nay kind of food to taste and also a good choice of drinks...something to visit if you are in Madrid!
Probably not as cheap as expected but the atmosphere is fantastic!

We went in twice on our visit to Madrid. The first time we bought cakes which were delicious and the second time was in the evening for a mooch about and buying snacks. It's so buzzy and colourful. All the food and drink look and smell amazing.

You have to visit if you come to Madrid.

Lovely building and so many food and drink options. The dessert stall with the meringue was amazing (€2.50). Beer is more expensive here but sangria and wine was a lot more reasonable. Would recommend looking around then finding a spot to sit and grab some drinks and tapas!

If your in Madrid make sure you pass by Mercado San Miguel its a very good way to introduce yourself to tapas and other food Madrid can offer, services are great. its easily located wit in Madrid and accessible.

Amazing market experience, great tapas and incredible variety. Architecture is a plus.
Can be hard to find a place to sit.
Not a huge market if if compared to Barcelona but lovely and compact . Diff food stalls from tapas to fruit and tables to sit and eat ( although quite busy). Would recommend a little stroll round :)
Great place but difficult to find a seat once you have a few tapas or whatever and it gets quite pricey very fast. Still. One of my favourite markets etc. Offering a bit of everything.
A special market space filled with food vendors of all types. Pick up some seafood, ham and burrata and wash it down with a libation of your choice. A delicious stop for all to enjoy.
Buzzing atmosphere. The ‘in place’ for locals and tourists alike. Great food, a variety of drinks, fantastic coffees, open the whole year round.

We found this place by accident, had a look around and vowed to come back when we were hungry. 24 hours later and we were back to enjoy good drinks, good food and good atmosphere.
You buy your drink from one place or another (beer, wine, aperol) and choose your food from a multitude of stalls and sit and enjoy yourself if you are lucky enough to get a seat, or stand by the windows which have a shelf by them. Great variety which can mean the evening can get a bit pricey but what the heck you're not going to be coming every night. One word of caution, watch your pockets - if you don't then someone else might help themselves to your tapas fund.
Will be back next time I'm in Madrid.

The market is very nice and has a lot of varieties of tapas .
I recommend you select some and have some wine with it as they do serve really good wines .

There are tables on the sides so you can sip your wine with those nice tapas .

Prices from 1-2 euros per tapas and the glass of wine was like for 4 euros .

The place is small and full of tastes.
Hou can nind sea food, meet, cheese and sweets, all are super decorated and full with special flavours.
It is a hive of activity, food and wine. See it on a Sunday where it draws crowds of Madridians. Tapas, jamon, boccadilos, wine and much more are on offer in abundance.

I love this place! It is like a small snapshot of Spain in one place at one time. The market is bright and bustling and all life is there. Choose from all kinds of mouthwatering tapas to sweet treats, from beers and wines to sherries and cocktails. The atmosphere is buzzing and the people watching is perfect.
We had a quick look around, the building and shops are really beautiful. We didn't try anything, it was really full and mostly meat/fish...

This is actually an indoor market with many food choices. Any kind of food you want. No place to sit though, you have to walk around and eat. Nice place to see what the area has to offer food wise. Paid $3 euro for a “ slider” mini burger
An education unlike no other. Step back in time and be overwhelmed by the number of tapas, wine and vermouth to try. A fun place to experience.

With it's historic iron signage Mercado de San Miguel transports you through a culinary adventure. It's an opportunity to taste your way through Spain without leaving the city limits of Madrid. The tapas are phenomenal, the staff are friendly and the feeling is energizing. It's a little touristy but well worth a visit!

I love visiting this place and is a must see to feel the vibe and see the food but beware that it was so crowded you couldn't move. The food looked great but most was a little expensive for me. Also, note that you must have your receipt in order to use the bathrooms in the basement (or pay for it's use).

A wide variety of high quality, excellent food. First place in Spain we tried so many different varieties of sangria. This place was definitely a favorite. We loved that most all of the food was sold in small portions so we could try a little bit of everything. Do not skip this place.

We got a reservation upon arriving in Madrid, recommended to us by good ol' Hemingway. We expected more touristy fare, and though there were plenty of tourists present, we were very surprised at the quality of the food. It's on the expensive side, but for the atmosphere and the quiet afternoon away from the noisy city, it was worth it.

We ordered the suckling pig and the artichoke hearts with ham iberico. The suckling pig was amazingly tender and juicy, with the skin roasted to a crisp. The sauce was simple, but it brought out all of the pig's flavor.

One word of advice: get a reservation, and try to reserve early (1pm) to avoid the afternoon lunch rush. You'll get a peaceful and delicious meal.

I wonder if restaurants that cater to tourists even bother to keep up to their standards. The staff was welcoming and attentive. The space is truly lovely. We ordered the special roast sucking pig and found it to be fatty, tasteless and totally unappealing. We also ordered some baby squid which was rubbery. I did see other diners who seemed to have no trouble with the food. Maybe our standards are too high. We live in NYC and are used to tasty, well prepared dishes. Although the waiters did offer for us to order other dishes, we declined. They were kind enough to deduct the cost of the food from our final bill.

I cannot understand why there seem to be so many ordinary reviews about this restaurant! My husband and I loved every morsel and minute of it.
The restaurant itself was amazing, the food excellent and the service first class. My husband had the suckling lamb and I ordered the suckling pig and both dishes were delicious - not salty but wonderfully flavoured. Our wine was exceptional - as all the wines have been so far here in Madrid.
This is a restaurant not to be missed and I cannot understand why Botin is being described as a tourist trap. When we went there for lunch it was packed to the rafters and everyone near us was a Spaniard, many business men.
If you miss this lovely restaurant because or some ordinary reviews it would be a great shame! Please go and enjoy - it is well worth it!

Lovely traditional cooked meals, making a nice change from tapas. We had the almond chicken and the garlic fried prawns which were both delicious, and a lovely cake for dessert. Food and drink were both reasonably priced for the quality. We also received free drinks from the waiter who was very attentive during our visit. Really enjoyable meal. We walked in and got a table but they only keep a small area free for walk ins so I would recommend booking.

This restaurant says it is the oldest in the world (and even has the Guinness book of records certificate in the window stating this!). Whilst it does have a tourist feel to it, the setting is in a pretty old fashioned Madrid building. Roast suckling pig was delicious. I would return.
Nice restaurant, lots of little cubby holes based in the cellar. Was not that keen on the suckling pig - the speciality - rest of the food very good.

Delicious food, nicely served in a wonderful setting.
The first time I dined at Botin, I was on my guard a bit, as it was praised in just about every guide book ... and Hemingway even mentioned it in The Sun Also Rises. It was superb several decades ago, and just as good this trip.
I and one other person in our foursome had their special Roast Suckling pig, and it was great. Others in the group enjoyed other good meals. I call it a "don't miss" part of a visit to Madrid.
Considered by Guiness World records to be the oldest continuously operating restaurant in the world [from1725 on].
Special tip ... tables can be reserved 3 months ahead of times on line, and it is an extra treat if you request to dine down in the "cave" below.

Founded in 1725 (I think) this is listed as the oldest restaurant in the world. Took a couple days to get in and overall was worth it. The roasted suckling pig was very nice. It is what they recommend and I loved it. Not life changing but worth the wait and now I can say I've been somewhere most people only read about. Service was great and is go again if I was in town.

Given it's the oldest restaurant in the world, one could be quite sceptical that it would be a touristic place.. Yet I must say the food was great (the suckling pig was so tender!) and the service was good too. It may be slightly over priced, but still worth a visit.. Pre-booking is recommended!

We were only in Madrid for 3 days, however this was the absolute best restaurant we ate at! The filet, was cooked perfectly without even asking how I would like it cooked. The only downfall is it was HUGE, it could have fed 3 people easily. We were so full by the time we were done with dinner we could imagine eating anything else until they showed us the dessert menu. Needless to say we left so stuffed and satisfied I would highly recommend eating here if you are in Madrid even if it's only for a day!

This is definitely something to check off from your gastronomic bucket list. It's the experience that makes it so fun. Our group had the two specialties (pig and lamb) and they were enjoyable but not insanely good. They are kind of like comfort food. I ordered asparagus - $20. This place is expensive but I think everyone should try it once just to visit the world's oldest restaurant! We were 4 adults and 5 kids and had a nice time - they are kid-friendly and gave coloring books and souveneir menus out.

Billed as the oldest restaurant in the world, this place caters mainly to tourists. But don't let that stop you. the food is excellent, make sure to order the suckling pig, and the atmosphere is incredible. I would certainly go here if I was visiting Madrid for the first time.

I remember ordering a pig and it came to the table head and all with eyeballs and an apple in it's mouth, and the waiters cut meat off the pig just by pressing against it with plates the meat was that soft and thoroughly crisped. It was very delicious and interesting. I was advised it was the oldest restaurant in the world.
This is the oldest restaurant of the world according to Record Guinness. The food is good but only to visit it once and to know the history
We loved the food and the atmosphere. Staff was very helpful accommodating a person in wheelchair at the table. Try ordering lamb as well. It is delicious.

This places is just great. The food was excellent, the staff very people oriented. We did not have any reservation and made the line with the luck to be able to enjoy a great evening. Totally recommend.

My partner and I dined here last night, we had a reservation booked and were looking forward to a dining experience. It was not that at all. The food wasn't terrible, it just wasn't good. If you want to visit the 'oldest restaurant in the world' come and view it, but DON'T dine here. The waiters could not care less, and it seemed that they couldn't rush through the service with us quick enough. No smiles, no effort, no conversation or ambiance. It's touristy and disappointing. I'm ok with paying for bread... But 2€ for butter to accompany it? It was packet butter. There are so many great places to dine in Madrid, don't waste your time eating here. I absolutely hate leaving bad reviews, I generally just brush off bad service, or bad food but as the whole experience was underwhelming and disappointing I felt that others needed to be warned off dining here if they were expecting it to be a great experience.

Would have given it more rating but...

Food was good, $$$$/4 price wise, service was ok prompt courteous but felt very impersonal and rushed. We were done within an hour. Yes they were like clockwork and robots but professionally dressed in white. Maybe cuz we were obviously tourists or maybe language Barrier. Would have gotten higher rating were it not for the service. Not friendly at all.

Had the calamari- one of the best we've had in Spain however at $21/plate it better be. Had the suckling pig of course- good, crispy -their signature dish. But we had the rear end half of the pig with tail and all -not what I expected. Yuck. Other table had the entire pig with head and all but that was a party of six. I know I've had better having eaten roasted pig often. In the end the suckling pig was good. Had the steak-good cooked perfectly. Had half chicken -good. Sangria-good. Marscapone dessert with mango-good. Apple tart-good typical with a little custard on the bottom. Madrid style special -puff pastry with custard filling sprinkled with powdered sugar-yummy good. Watch out-you're paying for the bread rolls which we didn't order and didn't know we had to pay for. Had we known we would have eaten all of the bread.

Oldest continuously running restaurant since 1725. Even In world Guinness record. We came for that and to show the kids and for our nostalgia many many many years ago although at the time we didn't know of its exalted standing and it wasn't as busy as this. So it was sort of our anniversary but it was not a romantic place for a date now. Menu has changed drastically. It use to have more items and of course was less expensive back then. We all knew about the fact back then that restaurant is famous cuz it's one of Hemingways fav and he mentioned it in a couple of his books.

We didn't see the other parts of the restaurant which we really wanted to.

WOULD RECOMMEND for the historical just to say you've been there. Somewhat for the food and somewhat for the service. Don't know if I'd necessarily go back as it truly has gotten busy, commercial, impersonal and capitalizes on its fame -plates jugs being sold Nickel and dime u on bread????? Really.

My wife and I visited the restaurant on Tuesday 8th, March 2016, as part of our mini break to Madrid. We had earlier done the walking tour of Madrid and the guide highlighted that the restaurant was the oldest restaurant in the World!. It certainly has a unique history. The staff at the restaurant were very helpful and the menu was extensive. The Sangria in the restaurant was outstanding.
The ambience is great - to be sitting in a 294 year old restaurant. However, the food is OK - a little over-priced for the quality of food.
I first went to Botin 54 years ago. It is still great. Delicious food and friendly staff made it a perfect present for me.

To be fair we also were able to have a short tour with the owner Antonio, so we may have a slightly different view of the restaurant now, but we ate lunch before our tour and thought the food was perfection. We had sangria and shared an order of the suckling pig, which is slow cooked in a wood oven (following a method since the inception of the restaurant). The result is tender moist meat with a crispy skin. I thought it was absolutely delicious with the sweet sangria, which comes in an attractive jarra which was perfect for two and also perfect for your Facebook photo :).

We learned from Antonio that the restaurant has been owned by only two families and his family has had the restaurant since 1930. He told us many of the staff have worked there all their lives. That says something about the restaurant's values and it comes through in the food. Under the restaurant is "secret tunnels" that offer an eerie peek into the underground tunnels of Madrid. I am not sure if they will let you look but there is no harm in asking :).

Don't miss out on this place even if its just to try the pig!!

We are a family of 9 people. We have no problem with our reservation. Food is simply the best in Madrid. Their oven baked suckling pig is well known . Now I know why. It's really mouth watering. Never ate such tender pork. The staff even gave us a tour of the Horno , (age old brick oven roasting , their wine cellar and the upper level section). Kudos to the chef and excellent wait staff . You made our vacation truly memorable.

We visited 5 years ago and skipped it this trip. As most people say, how was the food? In truth, its an experience in a place that claims to be the oldest continuously open restaurant in the world. Lots of charm and the food is good.

I suspect that if we'd booked in advance and had a table downstairs it may have been a more memorable experience but we walked in off the street and were put on the third floor where there wasn't a huge amount of atmosphere. Food was OK, suckling pig was very tasty but I wouldn't hurry back for more.

This was Christmas Eve we had made reservations 2 months before; for we did arrived that morning to Madrid and were 8 persons. This was the perfect choice, as always the service was very good, the house wine was also very good and the ( "cochinillo") roasted small pig was unbelievable and also the ( cordero helechal ) roasted lamb was an excellent choice remember that in Spain mostly everything is serve with potatoes. The deserts were also very good everything we had was very good from beginning to the end. Don't miss this historical restaurant in the center of Madrid. They also have a very good wine list and the prices are reasonable
The food was tasty (not the best I've ever had) but I enjoyed my meal here. The restaurant is very central and the portions are a great size.

One of the oldest restaurants according to the Guinness book of records. The service was amazing however i must say that i am not a fan of baby pigs and the menu and the food was too heavy for me. Overall it was a good experience but this type of cuisine it is not my type.

As someone who lives in Madrid full time- I took a visiting friend here so he could get the oldest restaurant in the world experience. I wasn't looking forward to the tourists.. but it was so professional and authentic! The service was amazing- even catered to my gluten allergy! We stayed for 3 hours and did not feel rushed. The food was AMAZING. Get the sangria and the chicken soup!

A must visit while in Madrid. It is the oldest known restaurant in the world. The food is quite incredible, specially the cochinillo. I recommend eating downstairs, however be careful as you go down the stairs that access the little dining area. Once you are downstairs, make sure to visit the little known antique cellar. It will be somewhat of a challenge to access the cellar but it is worth it. Lastly, ask to see the oven where the cochinillos are cooked. I highly recommend El Botin and believe you won’t be disappointed.

The ambiance is wonderful. If you have time this should be on your list of places to see. I would not say the food is wonderful. I ordered the lamb. It came with boiled potatoes. It was plentiful but not especially tasty. My wife ordered the pork, with boiled potatoes. It was nothing special when it comes to fine dining but certainly OK. The waiter was great. He was happy and joking and gave the impression he enjoyed his job and was happy we were dining there. The basement is more like a wine cellar in looks. In fact the wine cellar is there too and you can see it at the end of the cellar. The upper floors are decorated in tiles. The place is a joy to look at and the prices are not out of sight.

Part of the appeal is that it is a tourist trap -- the food is fairly priced and quite good. Dress up a bit -- slacks not shorts and you can get the prime spot on the second floor -- the restaurant is a bit of a labyrinth

This was on our list of must-dos in Madrid, as it is the oldest continuously operating restaurant in the world. Very unique atmosphere, charming old building with great history. The food was really good - we both had the suckling pig special, which comes with a half-bottle of wine, bread, and salad. The waiter threw in a few extras, too. Professional and understated service. Sure, it's a little touristy, but I wouldn't call it a "tourist trap". Enjoyable experience, overall!

We were with a tour group that took us there before their normal opening hours. Our entree choices were baked hake and beef stew that was so tender no knife was needed. Owners and staff very welcoming.
Worlds oldest restaurant and in the heart of Madrid. Intresting locals and decorations but most important, exelent food and service. Make you table reservations in avance!

As said, one of the oldest restaurants still operating in Spain so the ambience of this place was amazing. We had a reservation for 8 people but had 9 when we arrived and they were very gracious and accommodating. We had the most charming little room downstairs which we shared with another couple. The service and wine were excellent but the only reason this restaurant didn't receive 5 stars was some of the dishes were not top notch...for instance my veal was chewy. I will admit that none of us ordered their specialties. But overall, we had a very enjoyable dinner.

A must if you love cochinillo (roasted suckling pig) in what is said to be the oldest restaurant in the world. The roasted pig is the reason to eat here although they do have other choices on the menu. I have to admit that I had better suckling pig elsewhere in Spain but that was in Granada and in Segovia. The meat is delicious and tender with crispy (sometimes soft) skin. The place do have a lot of charm but be warned that this is a major tourist attraction and the place is swarming with American tourists. I would strongly recommend getting a reservation before hand. The service is prompt and friendly. The wait staff is very tourist friendly. Also this is not your place for a quiet romantic dinner as it can get pretty noisy with big tour groups. Having the right expectations, go and enjoy the cochinillo!

After almost 300 years of the same menu idea, they still maintain an amazing experience. We did the Botin Experience through Insiders Madrid and it was worth every penny. More food than two of us could hope to finish. Lovely building inside and out. The oven is the centrepiece. 10 feet of granite and coloured tiles

I have spent many special occasions at this historic eatery, where Hemingway penned his novels during the Spanish Civil War. It’s a bit touristy with lines of people waiting outside for the 8:00 pm sitting. Very few tourists wait until the 10:00 pm sitting. The key is to ask for the basement, much more intimate and private.

I’ve spent major birthdays there and the hospitality never changes. While the owner Don Antonio (whom I know)was not there on my last visit, his son was.
The cochinillo is always delicious and even more so is the Suckling Lamb(Cordero al Lechal). Alberto, my server on more than one occasion, didn’t remember me, but I jogged his memory. Many courtesies including birthday desserts were included as well as appetizers. Will always return.

This restaurant was highly recommended by a colleague of mine who studied in Seville. We had an amazing dinner in the basement to celebrate my 50th birthday. The service was excellent, including the manager who personally came around with a piece of celebratory cake to top off the perfect evening.

Reservations are recommended and the place was full for our visit!

The wait staff are accommodating and will speak English if you attempt some Spanish!

We sat down in the cellar which was air conditioned and great for atmosphere. Recommend the garlic scrimps, and of course the roast pork. The crema catalana and creme brûlée were great too.

Worth the visit.

We will post photos to our Instagram twofussyfoodies soon.

Had a great dinner here in a lovely historic setting. Billed as one of the oldest restaurants in the world that still operates you get a sense of history in it. Quirky stairs and one dining room you access through the kitchen adds elements of fun.
The food we had, suckling pig and garlic prawns were very well done.
Would strongly recommend a visit.

It's the oldest restaurant continuously operating in the world, according to the Guinness Book of Records. If it is "the oldest", everything else is irrelevant (or not). You can't have teh oldest restaurant in the world serving poor food. But the oldes does not mean the best... and certainly the less expensive. It's an experience. You don't want to be near by "the oldest" and not have lunch or dinner there...

Well below average food in an incredibly historic establishment. Doorman and Maitre ‘de were only interested in pushing tourists through as quickly as possible. Decent wait staff service, but nothing exceptional. Great atmosphere not matched by the food served. Seafood casserole, Prawns with Garlic, Veal Steak, and Chicken and Rice all underwhelming or outright lousy tasting. If you have to say you’ve eaten at the world’s oldest working restaurant, then go, but do so with low expectations.

Well, they say it is the most old restaurant in the world. What I can say is that you can eat exquisit plates and a wide range of wines in this place. It has floor level, two levels up and a basement where you can tell for sure it is a quite ancient building. Fantastic!

'The earliest restaurant in the world' according to the Guiness Books of Records, how tempting it is for us as tourists to visit and use it as the backdrop to our insta-selfie. It's the reason why we made a booking at Botin in the first place.

We were late for our reservation that evening and nearly at the point of giving up as we considered Botin as just another touristy spot or even worse, a tourist trap. We're late for about 30 mins when we finally arrived. However, after checking their reservation record, they were so accommodating that a table was arranged for us in the basement right away despite that the restaurant was indeed very full. The seating is tight and the tables are close to each other, which is similar to most old restaurants in Europe.

We didn't try the Cochinillo there as we were scared off by the one we had in Segovia that afternoon, bland meat under crispy skin, not our cups of tea.

We ordered Botin salad, Gazpacho, Jamon platter, baby squid with rice, Tarta Botin , creme brulee, vanilla ice-cream, 3 cokes and sparkling water which set us back €100, pretty reasonable to us. All dishes were simple yet delicious and tasted better than they appeared. The wait staff might be too busy to be attentive but friendly enough to accommodate your request and give you recommendations when asked. We loved the food there since it's less salty as in most restaurants in Spain and suited our palates more.

The door attendant was also very friendly and was more than happy to take a pic for us in front of the restaurant. It's an enjoyable evening and we didn't have a slightest feeling of being caught in a tourist trap.

Was there a couple of weeks ago. Had reservations for 8 pm. Told to be there 20 minutes early. It was raining and we had to wait outside in the rain. Promptly at 8 the door was unlocked and in a booming voice...."FORM A LINE". There must have been 20 of us waiting to enter......and we sort of lined up. We were taken into the restaurant, ordered the specials along with a truly mediocre bottle of wine. The waiter had no clue about the wines the restaurants serves. Price was reasonable and the food was nothing to write home about. Indecently, the Tour d'Argent restaurant in Paris has been around since 1582.

Beautiful setting. We were drawn to this place by its long history of operation and were pleasantly surprised to find the service and food were both better than one would expect at such a highly visited tourist spot.

3 of us dined for lunch on a weekday last week during vacay - made 1:00 reservations in advance which is a must! We did not experience any of the issues mentioned in the poor reviews. Our lunch/experience was perfect!! Had a delightful table (all the rooms are magnificent), service fantastic as was the food!! Prices higher but that's to be expected for this type of place and we went for special occasion. Location also great!! (tables are close together but didn't bother us - I knew this from pictures beforehand). Would definitely not miss this place and would return on future Madrid visits.

We booked this via a guided tour so had 1 hour tour of the building before having a set menu lunch. Excellent tour and the food was great. Good atmosphere. This is not fine dining and you won't get top quality presentation but you are eating traditional food.

Well, the Tapas in the bar were really good. Due to the move of the bar to a new location it's not the best place to sit outside now. I assume, that due to the good reputation in TripAdvisor we have seen koreans, german and other tourists but not so much spanish people. Food, Service are excellent. Very friendly, everything tasted fresh made.

For around 10 euros it is an excellent deal particularly cause the food is excellent! They include beer or drink, fresh bread (you have to ask for the butter), appetizers and dessert. The dessert they have tiramisu which you cannot miss! Homemade and fresh I would come here for the dessert alone. A must visit if you are within the atocha station area. It is between all three subway stations lavapies, Anton Martin and atocha.
Didn't bother looking at the menu. Told the waiter to bring me what he thought was good and he did a great job. The beef was AMAZING!

One of the best restaurants in Madrid! The food is delicious, with mixed dishes, rich meats and grilled vegetables. The service and employees are always attentive and friendly. Excellent price for amount and quality of food. Highly recommended for any night of the week.

A very nice place to go.
Very good food, very noce people.
I would have given 5 stars if the shrimps would have been great. But they weren't.
The calamari, the salads yes, 5 stars :)

Some one on trip advisor wrote that the ropa vieja here was the best food they had in madrid...that must have been after drinking four or five gallons of wine. Before I get to the ropa, let me flash back to the beginning. based upon the review about the ropa, my wife and I decided to try this place. we arrived and there were a lot of people already inside. all seemingly drinking and in high spirits. we walk in and were greeted warmly and taken to a table of two. the staff was great, polite and attentive. I loved them all. we ordered a bottle of wine which was delicious. no one rushed us. everything was great. my wife ordered what she thought was the Mediterranean salad, but maybe got confused and asked for the same salad the patron at the next table ordered. that salad looked fantastic. it turns out that the salad at the next table was not the Mediterranean salad, but the salad that had salmon. ok, it was still delicious. we also had the quiche with mushrooms. the flavor was very good, but I thought it was cold in the middle. the ends of the square piece of quiche that we got were warm or room temperature but the middle was decidedly cold, but who cares? we're on vacation, we have a bottle of wine to finish off. the vibe in the restaurant was hip and happening. all good. we order the ropa vieja and the risotto.

they brought out the ropa first. omg. the ropa was served on a plate with no rice, just chips, yes, freshly fried potato chips where some of the chips got stuck together and when you separate them, the part that stuck together is translucent...you know what I am talking about. thankfully, we ordered the risotto to go with the ropa. the risotto came out and it was inedible. I can only liken it to spackle. the consistency as unbelievable. I took a spoonful and turned it over and asked my wife how long she thought it would take to fall off the spoon. it took twelve seconds. the ropa, was brown and runny. the taste wasn't horrible, but the presentation was really sorry. after finishing our wine, we asked for the bill and paid and on our way out, the manager (I guess) shouted out not to leave, they wanted to give us a complimentary after dinner drink, which was soooo nice. (they had no idea we didn't like the food, we hadn't said anything.) like I said, I loved the staff, but the best food in madrid. errrr, there is a better place two doors down.

the fact that we found this other place while walking to taberna, made the evening worthwhile.

Everything was perfect here, the ambience was beautiful with dim yellow light and music. The service was excellent, John was very helpful in recommending dishes. After knowing it was my birthday, many staff came with a beautiful milk cake accompanied by a candle. They all sang birthday songs to me, which was very very sweet of them!! John even gave us some free homemade Spanish wine as Christmas presents! Not to mention the food and sangria were delicious! Definitely would come back again!!

11 of us art students were strolling on this road looking for somewhere to eat. The staff immediately noticed and invited us in to sit us at a large table.
• Well English speaking staff
• Clean toilets
• Appealing art and atmosphere
• Very efficient timing and service
• Complimentary olives, bread and olive oil, and shots
• enough space and well presented food and drinks
• Free Wifi
• Great meat options: steak, beef, chicken etc.
• A few vegetarian options: Stir fry, mushroom croquettes, goats cheese and tomato dish etc.

This little restaurant was recommended to us by the reception staff at our hotel and did not disappoint. We enjoyed several tapas dishes and a lovely bottle of local wine.
The staff were very helpful and happily looked after us very well. The food was very good as was the wine they recommended (after providing a few tastes for us)
Well worth a visit when you are in Madrid and would love to come back again to try some more of their well priced tapas.

We got to this place by accident, as it was close to our rental. First good sign was that the place was packed and mostly with locals, which is always awesome. Atmosphere was great, drinks arrived very soon and the food was great. Excellent place, staff was very friendly, definitely would recommend.

The Female staff speak fluent English and willing to give the recommendations based your need.
The rissto is really tasty and the cocktails is nice as well.
We really felt very warm and had a great time here.

This restaurant was truly amazing. We had dinner here two nights in a row and everything we ordered was exceptional. DO try the cod fish. Service and atmosphere were great. Prices very reasonable. Such a great restaurant!
Stopped in on our first day in Madrid after visiting the Sofia. The food was excellent, as was the service, extremely friendly. The tapas was varied and very flavorful.

I've never had a more positive experience in a restaurant in Spain than I've had at Más al Sur! The waiters were extremely attentive and friendly, and were understanding when due to unforseen circumstances I had to push the time of the dinner back a half hour on the day of the dinner. Más al Sur was a PERFECT place for my large birthday dinner, and I will be back many more times!! (Also, they have the best sangria I've found in Spain!)

Me and my wife visited the place around 6 pm after visiting the museum Reina which is close by. We were the only customers at the time, but people keep dropping in while we tried four different types of dishes : Risotto de Beloteus (Boleteus risotto with crispy ham, which we both can really recommend), Pechugas Al Curry (curry chicken), Ropa Vieja ( Cuban recipe of shredded flank steak) and Gambones (grilled prawns with garlic, which also was delicious if you like garlic). My wife had a Sangria which she also liked very much. Good service. Can really recommend.

We have had dinner there twice in the last week and enjoyed it immensely. It was recommended by our excellent hotel, the Artrip. Once we sat outside (only a few tables there) and the second time inside in an air conditioned room. The customers seemed a mix of locals and international tourists. We were made to feel welcome, despite our very limited Spanish. The waiter William was especially friendly. The food was good, especially the salmon, and the atmosphere was like a neighbourhood eating place rather than a tourist restaurant. It is by no means fine dining but gives excellent value. We would certainly go back next time we are in Madrid

As soon as you walk into this place, you notice the waiters/servers are just so really nice to you, so welcoming and pay attention to you like you're the queen of England! We were immediately seated, served with a basket of bread, given so much attention that we almost felt spoilt! We asked for a table outside but since one wasn't available, we were seated inside. However, as soon as an outdoor table became available, the servers immediately let us know and moved us outside. The sangria was good, the ropas veija was really yum, the risotto was nice (although I've had better), the salmon tartar was decent. On the whole, great service and good food makes me want to go back to this place again!

My wife & I went for a wander up the back streets behind the Reina Sofia Modern Art Museum in search of a great meal.

We chose this place at random . . . We weren't disappointed!

Tasty food, raciones sizing, with a reasonable drinks menu & efficient service.

Highly recommended!

Amazing quality food, best Sangria in the city and not expensive at all compared to any tourist trap! We came here multiple times during our visit, absolutely fabulous place topped up by second to none service. Andres was very welcoming and attentive! :)

We love this place and come here often. The staff, drinks, food and charm shines through the quiet street of santa isabel and has become our first choice of restaurant throughout the city (even better that we live round the corner). Without doubt, the staff are Madrid's finest and friendliest. The cocktails are beautifully presented (but I always get cava), and the menu is interesting and flavoursome (we have probably tried them all).

Thankyou for your hospitality, we will come again.
A group of friends were at noon. Vergilio met us and offered us an unforgettable experience with perfect food and service.
We had Prawn Risotto, Squid salad and Mushroom Risotto and it was amazing. Especially the prawns and squid were stunning. Also very nice and cozy place with pleasant service.
Went for a business meeting to Madrid and found this little restaurant. Very nice menu card and very taste full dishes.
We visited Mas al Sur with a group of 10 people, and were attended to very nicely by our host William. We recommend the place for food en service

We tried crunchy eggplant, ropa vieja, chicken curry, and squid salad. All were yummy and very filling. Really good old fashioned’s. Very friendly servers. If you don’t speak Spanish, Oswaldo’s your guy.

Found this restaurant on TripAdvisor and was not disapointed. Had to wait some time for a table because the place was packed. We enjoyed a fabulous cheese plate, wine, grilled octopus, steak, and shrimp risotto. Our waiter Yorbis was very helpful and funny. Definitely a great place to dine in Madrid!

Was directed here by one of their other restaurants and were not disappointed! Food was great, especially the risotto. Our waiter David was very attentive and helpful in explaining our options. Wil definitely go back should we visit Madrid again.

Food and service was great! Food was well presented, cooked perfectly, and had a lot of flavor. Sangria was awesome. Staff was very welcoming and friendly. Big shout out to dimar, Jorge, David, and Andres!!!

I had a great dinner experience with my father in Mas Al Sur. We had seafood paella and a steak and we both enjoyed our dishes. The customer service was extremely friendly and fast. Located in a nice area and the place has great atmosphere too. Would definitely recommend this place, thanks David and the rest of the staff!

Loved this place! My husband and I practically licked our plates clean! The musaka is good as well as the crujientes. We ordered the paella de mariscos and were not disappointed. We were well attended and were even given some freebies because it was evident we were so elated to be there. 10/10 would go again!
Great place, tasty food (prawns with garlic) good wine and really friendly waiters (thank you Edu, Rodri and Jonth :)). Surely I'll come back!

Me and my family had dinner here tonight. We were there around 21:00, and it was quite busy. Although we waited for almost 20 mins, the staffs were friendly and kept updating how long we should wait for.
Food portion is big, so I recommend people can share together, unless you are starving AFz.

I had steak and it was FABULOUS!
Tender and juicy, height recommend!

The staff, Johnny, provided us a lovey service and good English speaking. Other staffs also gave us a great night!
Just go. You won’t regret it. Take your friends. Your family. And go. Sangria, risotto, eggplant with honey... you can’t go wrong with anything. Enjoy!
Went w a group of 9 and it was amazing. Great portions and delicious food we would definitely return. The service was great too and the drinks looked amazing. Very happy customers
Really good food and really friendly staff. We had croquetas and empanadas and then our waiter gave us free shots and cheesecake. Definitely would recommend going.

On our recent trip to Madrid, this was one of our favorite places to eat. The atmosphere is fun with a mix of locals and tourists. We had to wait a few minutes to get a table since it was busy, but I took that as a good sign! The food was delicious and the wait staff was engaging, attentive and kind. We would recommend this restaurant to anyone who travels to Madrid. We'll most certainly go back next time we're in town!

During a recent visit to Madrid, we asked the hotel for a suggestion for dinner. This is where they went us. They marked it on the map.

The restaurant is a few blocks from the train stations, basically behind the art museum.

It’s a narrow, yet deep restaurant. It looks like it’s a local place. The décor was rustic, although we saw some recognizable Ikea furniture.

The place got packed quickly. Lots of folks like us, maps in hand, came in.

We were seated up front near the bar. There’s a high energy level. We had risotto, which was good. We also had a bottle of wine and a bottle of water. The bill came to about 34 Euros, which wasn’t bad.

Service was good.

Are there negatives? It’s hard to find. It didn’t appear that the house numbers worked the same way they do back home. I thought we were lost, then we found it.

I was in the area and thought I’d check it out! It definitely exceeded my expectations! I had the seafood paella. It was tasty and the portions were big, the bread was delicious and the cheesecake was superb! The non alcoholic cocktail, San Francisco was super good too! Excellent service! Super friendly staff! I will definitely come back here when I’m in Madrid!

Everyone loved it, the food is affordable yet very good. We recommend the paella and the shrimp with garlic, yum
People there are nice, thanks Yonathan for your service !

Truly my favorite spot in Madrid! The service of the staff is the nicest and family oriented service I’ve ever received. Not only did they go above and beyond their job of communicating well and ensuring we enjoyed our food and drinks, they were some of the warmest and friendliest people. If you want to welcome yourself to Madrid, this is the place to go. The food here is phenomenal - I’m sure as you’ve already seen in pictures and reviews from other people. I love eating the calamari and dipping bread in the white sauce that comes with it!

We had the best food and drinks during our trip to Madrid here. This place is casual and slightly off the beaten path (even though it is just a short walk from the Atocha station). We ordered empanadas, paella, and sangria. Everything was delicious. I have to say that the sangria was the best I have ever had in my life. Peter took care of us, and he provided excellent service to us and left us smiling at the end of our meal. We appreciated the homestyle feel and overall experience.

After I chose a seat, I was served immediately, the food was very good. There is a daily menu and a fixed one. The time until I got the food was appropriate, the style in which the food was presented on the plate was nice and food was fresh and tasted delicious. The personnel speaks english in case you dont understand.
Great options for both meat eaters and vegetarians. The tempura salmon was amazing. The morning team looked after us and even gave us a complimentary shot. Definitely worth a visit

The risotto with fried ham and grilled baby squid were fabulous! It is a must to dine here while in Madrid!

Dimar was very attentive as well!

We just finished our meal at Mas El Sur right around the corner from our AirBnB. Some reviews have accused this place of paying for ads. We are not being paid. We order drinks, tapas and a main meal. To be honest the main meal did not arrive until after we received our check. We were ok with this since we were very full. We did not accept the main course and there was no trouble. The price was taken off our bill and the restaurant gave us an after dinner drink and dessert on the house. This is about customer service and Mas El Sur made it right. The Sangria was very good with a very nice local atmosphere. We would go back and would recommend this place.

Our second time at Mas al Sur and we loved it! Great service, especially from Anthony, Dimar, Alejandro, and Luis the sangria is divine and the cheesecake always leaves me wanting more. The paella is fresh, calamari also delicious.
We had the best last meal before we departed back to the US at Taberna Mas Al Sur. Daniela was an incredible waitress and made our day! Thank you for the wonderful experience!

We came here because we saw good reviews and we were not disappointed. We weren’t completely sure what food to order and our waiter Johnny helped us choose, he was very helpful and talkative. The food was great and the sangria certainly didn’t disappoint either. We’d recommend you to order several half portions and share the food with your group.
Gracias!

Everything was great from drinks to food, especially the sea food paella was divine, tasted so good and sweet shots after dinner was a surprise (tasted like icecream). Special thanks to Emílian and His colleagues for their hospitality.
I am used to eating only cheese burgers because I am American, so this blew the beans out of my underpants. The food was very good and they gave us free shots, so it’s a win win.

We were hustled in by an employee, promising two free drinks. A three course set menu was promised. We went for a 30 euro tapas selection which included sangria as the menu was the day menu (we went at 8pm and it was still out). Never got free drinks. Sangria was good but came in a high narrow carafe, which was very difficult to pour and I made a mess. The napkins we used to mop the spill up were left in our table the entire time and we didn't get any new ones. The tapas arrived one by one, the last one with a break of a good 10 minutes. It was cold (croquetas). We only had forks, no knifes to cut chicken or spoons to use for sauces. Not a lot if food for the money, a trip to McDonald's on the way home in order. Quite disappointed.

We were lured into this place with the idea of fresh food at a good price.
Neither were true.
It really is a tourist trap; with tourist guides bringing groups of people and sell the "home made paella".

Really not worth it.

Tip: if you are near the area, walk 2 blocks over to Huertas. It is packed with a bunch of good places to eat.

We found this place on tripadvisor, and as reviews were good, decided to try it. They had good meal deal offers, and food itself was good, I can say very good. The trickiest part was to order this food. The were 5 waiters on the time of our visit, and only one of them was able to speak English. After she took order from my friend and ignored me, I had to wait for 20 more minutes to order food. I felt a bit disappointed.. I understand that I'm visiting foreign country, but still expected that I will be able to get my food without Spanish language knowledge.

i find everything good about this one. their paella is yummmm.. i have been there twice during my 1 week trip to madrid. with my friends we have tried a few of their a la carte.. all were excellent.. you would miss something if you don't try their desserts.
Good value for money n good quality as well , the service was good , they recommended the squid n was good.................

We were walking around Sol, looking for a place to have dinner, and a public relations guy talked us into visiting this place. The menu was quite limited and poorly translated. For dessert they had like 6 options but only 2 or so were available. The waiter could have been more friendly. The food was incredibly amazing and tasty.

I was looking for lunch when I found this restaurant on Tripadvisor. I was offered a lunch set which consists of the first course and the main dish including desert and drink. There were various choices of menus which you can choose and it was only for 12.99 euros.

I ordered a paella for the first course and a beef steak for the main course, which was quite good but the meat was a bit overcooked than what I ordered.

And the staffs very nice, great service!

I really enjoyed this restaurant. It was a little tricky to find but we got there. We got a seat upstairs, it wasn't until much later i realised that the downstairs was much bigger and the place was packed.

We had the paella which was gorgeous, it was explained to us that it would take around 40 mins to cook but no problem we were not in a hurry. While we waited we were brought tapa of potato wedges which were yummy.

I loved the atmosphere of the places too it had a really cool vibe to it.

Topped off perfectly with some great cocktails!

Thumbs Up!

The restaurant has staff waiting outside to lure you in. It has a great trip advisor rating as well. However the food was not great. We got a couple of tapas and the beef steak for 2. The beef was good but tapas were mediocre. The sangria was watered-down and service took very long.
We might have caught the restaurant on the wrong day but it was below expectations

We were looking for a good place to eat in the close proximity to Gran Via and Sol. We found this place on trip advisor and decided to give a try based on its high reviews. What we found when we got there was a lovely place, warm and cozy with friendly and helpful staff that speaks English and absolutely delicious and fairly priced food. Wide selection of tapas in vegetarian, vegan and meat options. I recommend octopus, mushroom soup, mince meat filled peppers. We will be definitely coming back there. Thank you for a great experience.

this venue was included in the sandemans tapas tour .. well worth going ; lovely staff and tapas were very good .it looked like there was a queue to get in so might be best to book as it seems very popular .
Lovely characterful restaurant. Typical spanish food, plenty of it. Tapas to start then paella and steak. Strongly recommend a visit.

Tx to good reviews in tripadvisor, we found this place..it is tucked in a small alley just off the central of Plaza Mayor. All tge waiters were very friendly and spoke good english. They had an English menu as well which was very helpful. We had the Seafood Paella and all the house specialties tapas, cant remember all d names but they are at the bottom right hand corner of menu: aubergine, cheese and arugula salad (with a very interesting dressing injected with huge needle into the cheese), jamon croquette, pork escalapoe, tuna tataki. Everything so yummy we basically finished the whole thing between 2 adults and 2 children.
On the way out my husband accidentally broke a wine glass but the waiter said not to worry at all, human made mistakes with a big smile. Have not encountered such nice service and friendliness in other establishments in Madrid so far!

As a first time traveller to Spain, I thoroughly enjoyed the authentic cuisine, and warm atmosphere. The staff are excellent, and I had the pleasure of receiving great service from Alejandra twice. I hope to make it back again.

Tapas available to go? YES!
We had an airbnb 2 around the corner and didn't feel like eating out. I saw the TA ranking and great reviews of this place, thought I would walk down andask if they offer to-go. And yes they did, everything on the menu but cocktails...

Servers were very very nice and accommodating.

Had the eggplant chips, they were delightful, wife felt there was a little too much sauce, but other than that, they were really good.

There was a beef tapa, which essentially was a flank steak with some salad, it was really good, with a good 4-5oz of steak, could not believe it was sold at tapas price. This was their recommendation.

Finally patata bravas. Nicely done with a delicious sauce.

Will definitely go back next time for a sit down meal!

Amazing food, great drinks and sangria. For about 35 Eur we ate amazing (and a bit to much) gor 2 people. Great and friendly service from Lara!
I will be be back and can absolutly recommend others to visit!

Visited after reading good reviews on trip advisor and did not regret it. We ordered around 5 different tapas dishes all very reasonably priced. All the dishes were great value for money and the restaurant had a good atmosphere too. Good little find!

Definitely the best meal we had in Madrid. Awesome Tapas. Great service. Lovely atmosphere and good value. Albariño wine @ 11€ a bottle. Really tasty food, super desserts and great espresso. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend

This restaurant was really close to our hotel in plaza Sant'Ana. Prices were very reasonable with attentive service. The restaurante has a great rustic atmosphere and the menu offered lots of tapas.
Croquettes were delicious and the burrata had pesto sauce inserted on. It was so tasty.

Had a meal here with friends on a busy Saturday night. Had various small dishes and paella. Great service from David and Laura. They looked after us well. Would definitely come back. Tuna fish was superb.

Visited whilst on holiday in Madrid for a week. The service was great and the food was excellent. Tapas can get a bit boring after while but this place gave it a modern twist. The mozzarella with pesto was beautiful, the aubergine and honey crisps were lovely - we enjoyed all of the food.

It's tight quarters, but that's partly because it's a party that everyone wants to be a part of. They were turning people away, so we were grateful just to get in after a bit of a wait, and the experience didn't disappoint. The food was excellent, with special kudos for the paella and the smoked octopus -- but everything was very good. And bonus points for being casual and fairly priced!
the menu had good variety, we had beef, chicken, sardine, eggplant and octopus to share. It was very good. service was good and quick as well. English menu and spoke English well
This restaurant is really amazing! Food looks and tastes great! Staff is very kind and helpful,moreover everything was served quickly! Big thanks to Monty - he’s the best waiter ever!

We were looking for a place to fill up on some tapas and decided to give this one a shot because it was rated well, and it did not disappoint!
We got a big selection of foods, all of which tasted amazing, and was great value. The waiter, Monty, absolutely rounded off the experience - he was extremely friendly, professional and efficient, with an impressive memory (he took the orders for our table and the one next to ours by memory, and not a mistake!). He was very thoughtful with the bringing out of dishes as well, so we were only working on 2 dishes at any time, ensuring we got hot, freshly-prepared tapas the whole meal through.
We had the patatas in alioli sauce (large), the truffle omelette, chicken wings, croquettes (small), pork loin, and two of the tropical mocktails between 2, and we were absolutely stuffed at the end. You could easily fill up for under 15 euros per person (we went harder and spent about 20 each), and it was absolutely delicious. The croquettes and wings especially stood out for me, but I thoroughly enjoyed every dish.
Would highly recommend for anyone looking to get some excellent tapas for a great price, and with absolutely brilliant service!

Defo worth a visit. Been here a few times and all the food and dishes are lovely, full of taste & well presented. White sangria is good too, aswell as cocktails! The only thing is the menu isn’t very big & there isn’t a great deal of options but it is defo worth a visit. All the staff are very attentive and helpful

I booked online but when we arrived there was no room for us and we were told to wait outside along with lots of others also waiting to get in. It didn't seem to matter that we had a reservation. The restaurant seemed to be understaffed and the waiter seemed stressed and a little rude. The food was nice but there are plenty of nice restaurants in Madrid...

Food was great and nice atmosphere!
Good selection of choices, although a bit more choices would have been good as well!
Thank you Ianko for your service!

I had booked this restaurant as it had been recommended by a travel guide book. We were seated at a downstairs table after a short wait. The atmosphere was lively and buzzing. My friends and I decided to order from the tapas menu so that we could share. The food arrived fairly swiftly in plates of twos. We were not disappointed. The calamari in little dumpling tacos were absolutely delicious! The rest of the meal that followed equalled the high standard of that first plate. Wine was exceptionally priced at 13€ and was lovely. The whole evening was very enjoyable and I would highly recommend this restaurant to any visitors to Madrid. Thank you to the owners for a great evening.

Food was really good just let down by the service, which is a shame as we had prebooked on the basis of a friends recommendation.

Firstly, didn’t bring out one of our dishes, then when it came we had someone hovering over shoulder waiting for us to finish.

Then, before we had finished we were told we had to move table due to another booking when want to order desert and a second round of drinks. Left a bit of a sour taste after the food.

If you want a lesiurely dining experience, I wouldn’t recommend it. However, if you want to be in and out within an hour this may be the one for you.

My friends and i are searching for a good resto around the city of Madrid and i consulted this apps for a good resto, La rosi loca has an ups and down but we gambled everything to try this place, other dishes is like a normal taste but the presentation of the food is top, we ordered one dish per head and paella dish with seafoods. The dishes that we ordered per head is above the average in their taste and good presentation of the dishes for this matter i like to give them but the paella seafoods taste below the poor rated, i didnt like the way they serve it coz you can count the seafoods like 4 pieces of shrimps and 4 pieces of mussels and some cuttle fish that cut into small pieces. My friend ordered the tataki atun (in other language is just only a seared tuna with teriyaki sauce and a white sauce) i dont know why they have it on their menu using the teriyaki sauce so its mean that its not totally an spanish resto. Another thing, as we pass by to pay at the cashier we thought that the Sangria is home made but my friend saw it that they use the bottle sangria(the one that you can buy in the market) and pouring it into the carafe/pitcher added with some fruits and ice, so if youre thinking to get the sangria ill recomend you to buy it on the bar where you can see the barista’s working it by their hands and not an industrial hand. In overall ratings ill recomend you to try other resto to find a good paella and good Sangria hope they realize that the costumers has a high expectation when its come for the food and beverage section

Godbless
Very nice location, the tapas are the best we have tried during our trip, the waiters are very friendly (esp. Ana and Alex ); all in all a great, recommendable restaurant

Our waiter Richard made us feel really welcome with recommendations for different dishes from a great tasting menu. Exquisite tastes, however, a single person paella would be an added choice on the menu.

Nearby is plenty of other restaurants, but this is normally full.
Small and funny: it seems like the Rain Forrest inside.
Food is typical Spanish with tapas, sangria and paella (3 kind of paella).
Price is good: about 25€ for person eating 2 tapas, 1 paella for 2 and 1 later of sangria.

Recommended.
Super friendly and helpful staff. The accommodated our 1 year old son amazingly. The food tastes amazing and it was presented with fun flair and care. We had the paella, house lemonade and sangria.
Amazing menu with many quirky Spanish dishes at a very affordable price. Staff are always lovely even though it is always very busy! Love the decor.

It appeared to be a popular place due to the amount of people in there, we were very happy to get a table! Richard was our waiter and he was amazing!! He was so welcoming, friendly and assertive. The food was delicious and the overall experience was great. After asking, we received recommendations from Richard about where to go in the city, he was very helpful, he gave us contact cards and wrist bands to get into certain places for free, we were very grateful. Thank you Richard!

The Tapas, service and atmosphere in Rosi la Loca is just exceptional! We didn’t have a reservation but they were more than happy to accommodate us even though they were fully booked for the evening. All our tapas was simply gorgeous especially the Tuna Teriyaki.
Richard our waiter was fabulous and couldn’t do enough for us!
6 large tapas dishes and 6 large glasses of sangria for €60 was worth every single cent! Highly recommended this place and would definitely return!
Thank you Rosi la Loca for a wonderful evening
We went for the paella. It was horrible. Undercooked, no flavor. Sangria was great. That’s about it....tourist trap. Not sure how it got good reviews.

We went here for lunch at 12:30 and were the first clients.
Nice (a bit crazy decorated...) location and very friendly people.
We had a few tapas all fresh made and they were delicious - all of them!
After a short while this place was packed with people and outside a long waiting queue. Don't panic and finish early because of that - this happens almost every day...!
This is not only a cool location with nice and friendly people but the food is really good and you get a lot of value for the prize you pay. Much more than in many other places in Madrid!!
For us this location was one of the best lunch-/dinner places in Madrid's centre.
If we come back to Madrid we will come back to this place - for sure.

Rosi la loca team - you rock!
Thanks for this wonderful moment today!

Checked Trip Advisor to find out where to find good paella for dinner & came across Rosi La Loca, a small restaurant decorated in vibrant colors with a bird cage-like structure at the entrance! The place preferred reservations but our family party of 4 went there at 6:30pm on a Friday evening and was told that if we could finish the food by 8pm because of no reservation made in advance, we could have a table right away...of course we settled. Ordered one each of the paella for two since we have 4 people in the party. One was seafood and the other was surf & turf paella! We received an appetizer of French fried with spicy sauce which was very good stomach teaser! Both paella’s were quickly consumed because they were very good. We finished the meal 1/2 hr before 8pm and were happy that we tasted paella as well as quite good food too!
Best restaurant I've came across in Madrid, if we would've stayed longer, would have had repeated visits. Remember to book ahead. The paella it's better than what I had in Valencia
Wonderful fusion tapas, superb eclectic surroundings and the best service in Madrid from Mauricio! Try the beef cheek bao buns and the croquettas both to die for ❤️

Best meal we had in Madrid during our 3-day city-break. The crispy, honey glazed aubergine and the burrata cheese, injected with some green deliciousness through a giant syringe were both delicious. Service was excellent - absolutely service with a smile. From what I could make out, almost every table was reserved so advanced booking recommended.

We went there looking for a paella and we were not disappointed - great food, original serving style, everything was very tasty (we had the tuna tataki, some calamari, croquettes and the seafood paella), the staff was friendly. Definitely recommended!

After eating in a number of different restaurants, we stopped here for our final meal before our flight home later that evening. We had tried to get a table the night before but with good reason, there were no tables available and we ended up in for a lunch time service instead.
We were served quickly - a pitcher of Sangria gave the 3 of us 2 glasses each for 15euro and we each ordered two mains each which was more than enough for lunch! We managed to squeeze in deserts (two between us) and were pleasantly full.
We had the pork tacos, ham croquettes, broken egg timbale (incredible and soooo filling), and the bloody rosi burrata. All of which were delicious and served equally as quirky as the restaurant itself.
Very glad we visited!

We loved the food and presentation. Everything was absolutely delicious from drinks to dessert. Reservations were fully booked so we waited about 40 minutes to sit outside on a Monday evening. It was worth it.

Absolutely gorgeous and delicious bites. So happy to have amazing decor and equally good food. Service was fantastic.
Make reservations as we saw the line started to get very long outside.
We made reservations right when it opened so we had a great spot.
Music was amazing too so we had a great sing a long.

Was told about this place and reserved my table 2 months in advance of my visit. So glad I did. This places is amazing, the food a dn drinks are delicious, the ambience is marvelous, and the staff very helpful. I loved everything about this place. Will deffinitively return when I'm in Madrid.
Fab cocktail place. So novelty and fun. Gets really booked up though so recommend to book in advance or you’ll have to wait outside for a table, which we did. Wasn’t too long of a wait!

We visited this restaurant on a Thursday night and had a great meal. We tried many dishes and they were all deliciious. We really enjoyed the Pulpo a la Gallega and the Merluza were especially excellent. Our server Antonio did a tremendous job in taking care of us. Highly recommend this restaurant.

I can not emphasis this enough....you will have an amazing experience at this restaurant.

The staff were incredibly welcoming, and keen to provide recommendations and suggestions. This isn't an order and eat kind of place, they want to make it a special and unique experience for their customers.

The food was incredibly tasty, the cocktails and wine were also a delight.

Will be coming back for sure!

Muchos gracias
Lovely food and wine, great atmosphere and brilliant service. Perfect evening meal made fantastic by the quality of the service and the timing of each course. The summer menu is a must.

Had a business meeting come dinner here and had a simply fantastic meal. They are celebrating their anniversary this month and offer a fantastic menu of a range of mixed starters and main courses with a bottle of wine per person for €55 a head. This is great value considering the quality of the food and wine. Our waiter - Ricardo was excellent and looked after us very well and made the meal more enjoyable with his easy manner and good suggestions. A very good meal and very good surroundings - highly recommended!
My wife and I came here for dinner after seeing the high rating on TripAdvisor. It is in a quiet area of Madrid but the food was very good

My friend and me were in Madrid to spent last weekend with some friends. Before leaving on Sunday, we wanted to treat ourselves, so we were looking for the best food. We called the restaurant if was a table available, good thinking, is so busy. Really kind the staff help us with ours suitcases. While waiting for our table we had drinks in the bar area with a handsome waiter, Alejandro <3

Kind Daniel bring us a fruity albariño, so we could start to look the menu. Alejandro always courteous, surprised us with a nice appetiser.
We share salmon with a delicious rice cream and caviar, simply marvelous, and Iberian secret with smoked salt of holm oak, also splendid.

We are from Galicia, and both with a good appetite, so we can't leave without trying a dessert, our choice was the Galician cheese cake, so yummy!!
Antonio was taken good care of us with some coffee liquor and others special treats! We really have a good time, they've been really delightful!

The restaurant has a modern decoration in blue that make you relax and enjoy the happy atmosphere, surprised us how big was and how many clients were enjoying Galician food.

Overall consistent quality and a MUST if you are looking for good food, best service and enjoy Madrid's life.

Saw the reviews and decided to give the restaurant a try during our most recent trip to Madrid. Made a reservation for two on Saturday night. We showed up 20 mins early to partake in some pre-dinner cocktails; upon greeting us at the entrance, Antonio and his staff seated us promptly without hesitation. While taking a look at the menu, we sampled a starter consisting of guacamole and salmon that was absolutely amazing! Having the Solomillo as our main dish (in addition to being cooked perfectly) our dinner was paired very nicely with a red wine highly recommended by the staff who were also very attentive in making sure we were as comfortable as possible. The night without a doubt, far exceeded our expectations! A big thank you to Antonio and his staff!

I would highly recommend this restaurant to those who want quality food and impeccable service!

Excellent resto serving typical food from Galicia region. All fresh and top quality, nicely presented, with a modern a sophisticated touch. Lunch menu is a great value quality price opportunity! The menu a la carte is just fantastic! Unforgettable service. Thank you, Antonio, for your wonderful service.

The Bar:
The bar keeper had a hard time distinguishing between a Hendricks martini and a Gin & Tonic. The result is that you receive something in between. Not a very interesting pre dinner starter.

The restaurant:
The two main courses are served with a 37 min interval. The guest are sitting twinning their thumbs awaiting the last course so they can dine together.
Drinks are referred after 21 min.
This is extremely amateurish and unlike anything I have ever experienced.
It's a complete fail. The pizza parlor down the street served us in a correct manor. Only cost € 7 too...

Madrid is a great city to eat. It may have the best food all around and with the best prices for the quality of food. Montes de Galicia was my last stop on my 3 week trip and boy did it pay off. Quality of food is superb and the service is top class. The place was easy to find and it's close to plaza de toros in ventas. Highly recommend the place.

We had a great talk with the service here - and then they gave us free coffee-flavoured cocktails at the end of the evening ! Surprisingly, this blend was very tasty. Great guys ! Thank you for the memory !

I went to this restaurant with my family for my 21st birthday and had one of the best dining experiences I've ever had.
